Title: Did Amrika promise Morocco's independence? The nationalist movement, the Sultan, and the making of the 'Roosevelt Myth'
Institution / publisher: The Journal of North African Studies 19:4, 524–539
Archival reference: State Department records; diplomatic cables and consular reports; photographs of Roosevelt's letters to Sultan Mohammed ben Youssef; White House press statements; nationalist documents; al-'Alam and al-Istiqlal.
Bias notes: Careful and even-handed: it neither endorses the nationalist myth nor dismisses it, arguing the promises were real and their political use was constructed. Written from a US-Moroccan relations vantage point.
Covers: Anfa, 22 January 1943. Moves this workspace's 'what did Roosevelt say' question from Unknown to Established-with-wording-unverified.

Title: FO 413 — Foreign Office: Confidential Print Morocco and North West Africa
Institution / publisher: The National Archives, Kew — 150 volumes, open
Archival reference: FO 413. Covers Morocco throughout; extended to Algeria and Tunisia from 1952.
Bias notes: British state reporting, with British interests — an active Moroccan policy until 1904 and Mediterranean and Gibraltar interests thereafter. But Britain was not a claimant in Morocco after 1904, which makes it the nearest thing to a disinterested European observer of Franco-Spanish conduct.
Covers: A curated printed chronological digest of British reporting across 130 years, including Foreign Office 'descriptions of leading personalities'. The most efficient single entry point to third-party evidence in the entire workspace.

Title: Deadly Embrace: Morocco and the Road to the Spanish Civil War
Archival reference: Built on Spanish, French and British archives; the source of the Berenguer 'con verdadera fruición' quotation used in this workspace.
Bias notes: Rigorous and archive-based. Its thesis — that the Rif war formed the officer corps that made the 1936 coup — is an argument, well supported but an argument. Written from a Spanish-history vantage point; Moroccan agency is present but not the primary subject.
Covers: Rif war; Spanish chemical weapons; the africanista officer corps; Annual; Abd el-Krim. The single most useful secondary work for Phase V.

Title: Ottoman Empire and Moroccan Resistance to the French Protectorate in the First World War: Activities of Teşkilat-ı Mahsusa in Morocco
Bias notes: Turkish scholarship working from Ottoman state records, so it reports the operation as its organisers saw it — including their own assessments of German interference. That vantage point is precisely its value: it is neither French nor Moroccan. Its judgement that the operation 'achieved unconventional war objectives' is an interpretation.
Covers: Emir Abd el-Malek; Taher Bey and the Ottoman officers; Moulay Abdelhafid's Barcelona negotiation 1915; al-Hiba; Raisuni; Moha ou Hammou; Sheikh Sharif ben Seddik; German funding; submarine and false-passport routes. The source of the first document-level archival references in this workspace.

Title: Hazine — guide to archives and libraries of the Middle East and North Africa
Bias notes: Practical researcher-written guidance rather than scholarship. Access details change; verify before travelling.
Covers: Concrete, current access information for Archives du Maroc, the BNRM, the Hassaniya palace library and the Direction des Archives Royales: opening hours, permit requirements, fees, photography rules, catalogue quality. The source of the access details recorded in the Archives & repositories database.

Title: Lords of the Atlas: The Rise and Fall of the House of Glaoua
Bias notes: The source of much of the English-language image of the Glaoua, and a book written with novelistic technique. Several of the most-repeated anecdotes — the 1893 Telouet rescue, the Krupp cannon, the details of El Glaoui's vice interests — trace back here. Compelling, influential, and not a substitute for documentation. Flag every claim that depends on it.
Covers: Madani and Thami El Glaoui; the High Atlas; the 1953 deposition.

Title: Alta Comisaría de España en Marruecos (fonds record)
Institution / publisher: Archivo General de la Administración, Alcalá de Henares; catalogued in PARES
Archival reference: AGA, Fondo África, 1.2.5.1 Órganos Centrales — Alta Comisaría de España en Marruecos. 4,990 cajas.
Bias notes: The administrative record of the Spanish protectorate, produced by it. Uses 'cabecilla', 'rebelde', 'bandido' as classifications of Moroccan political actors. Also contains the output of Moroccan officials in Spanish service — including Abd el-Krim before 1915.
Covers: The core Spanish holding for the Rif war, the Jebala, Tetouan, northern nationalism, and the whole protectorate administration. Box-level references NOT YET VERIFIED.

Title: al-Wathā'iq (« Les Archives ») — published Makhzen documents
Institution / publisher: Direction des Archives royales marocaines, Rabat
Archival reference: Periodical volumes of documents published from the Royal Archives.
Bias notes: Selected and published by the Moroccan state, with an emphasis on pre-colonial international relations — that is, on the material that supports Moroccan sovereignty claims. Selection is itself an argument. But it is Makhzen documents in the original, which is what this workspace has been missing entirely.
Covers: The single most important corrective available to this workspace. Makhzen correspondence in Arabic, published and therefore accessible without a palace reading-room permit. The obvious first target for anyone continuing this work.

Title: SHD — Guide des sources sur le Maroc (sous-série GR 3H)
Archival reference: Sous-série GR 3H, c. 3,000 articles. Commandement Supérieur 3H 314–752 (1st–4th bureaux; Fes, Meknes, Marrakech, Taza, Tadla, Oujda). Goums 3H 2375–2711 (1906–1958). Ministerial cabinet telegrams on Morocco in série N at 5N 39–64.
Bias notes: A finding aid produced by the institution that generated the records. It describes what France chose to keep and how France classified it — e.g. 'affaires indigènes', 'dissidence'. Its categories are evidence about the Protectorate's mind, not neutral description.
Covers: The single most important French holding for Moroccan military and Affaires Indigènes history. Series-level ranges above are from the guide itself; individual carton references remain NOT YET VERIFIED.

Title: Abdelkrim, Mémoires d'Abd el Krim
Author / producer: Mohammed ben Abdelkrim El Khattabi; edited by J. Roger-Mathieu
Bias notes: Use with care. A Moroccan leader's account, produced in French, through a French editor, in the year after his surrender and while he was in French custody or exile. The mediation is heavy and the editorial agenda is not neutral. It is nonetheless one of very few first-person Moroccan sources for the Rif war.
Covers: Abd el-Krim's own account of the Rif war and the Republic.

Title: Inventaire des archives du Maroc — sous-série 3H
Archival reference: Organised geographically: Région de Marrakech (1916–1955); Territoire de Ouarzazate (1929–1956); Cercle du Dadès-Todhra (1936–1956); Cercle de Zagora (1928–1956); Territoire du Tadla (1909–1956). Personnel dossiers 1929–1956; confidential outgoing-mail registers from 1929.
Bias notes: Same caution as the guide. Note that the geographic hierarchy — région → cercle → bureau/annexe → chronological — is itself the shape of French administrative control, so the archive is easiest to search in the terms France used.
Covers: Regional political reports, tribal intelligence, situation reports, indigenous affairs, operations, personnel. Essential for El Herri, the Zaian war, Bougafer and the pacification generally.

Title: Moroccan Resistance, Pan-Islam and German War Strategy, 1914–1918
Archival reference: Uses French and German archival material.
Bias notes: The standard treatment of the German and Ottoman effort to raise Morocco against France during the First World War. Assesses that effort as largely ineffective — a judgement worth testing against German records directly.
Covers: Zaian war context; German funding via Madrid (figures up to 600,000 pesetas a month appear in this literature); Ottoman training and propaganda; attempts to use Abdelaziz and Abdelhafid as figureheads.

Title: Expediente Picasso
Archival reference: The inquiry file into the Annual disaster. Location and completeness of the original NOT YET VERIFIED by this project.
Bias notes: A state investigating its own catastrophe, under political constraint. It named military failings and was structurally unable to reach the crown. Its casualty total of 13,363 is the highest in circulation and is the most inclusive definition, not necessarily the most accurate.
Covers: Annual, July–August 1921: command failures, positions, testimony, casualty returns. The primary documentary base for the disaster.

Title: Ottoman Support to Moroccan Local Resistance in North Africa (1914–1918)
Archival reference: Cites BOA HR.SYS. 2392/2, 2393/1, 2393/2, 2393/4; German A.A.-P.A. WK Nr. 11 1.
Bias notes: French-based scholar using Ottoman and German archives — a useful cross-check on Kaya, and the two differ on a point of fact (whether Abd el-Malek was Abd el-Kader's son or grandson), which is exactly why both are recorded.
Covers: Teskilât-ı Mahsusa structure and personnel; Abd el-Malek's c. 1,500 fighters from March 1915; the Madrid and Barcelona rear bases; German payment of 70 liras monthly per officer from Nov 1916; the Ifni submarine expedition of Oct 1916; Salah Sharif at-Tunisi's pamphlets in French, Arabic and Tamazight.
